subject.title: Feature Request: Masked Secrets - Prevent Agent from Accessing Raw API Keys

question: Should OpenClaw make a scoped credential broker the first supported core boundary for agent-executed capabilities, or keep agent-exec credential isolation outside core/plugin deployments?
rationale: Current protections reduce accidental disclosure but do not isolate a credential from code running in the same agent process; deciding the supported trust boundary determines whether core, plugin SDK, or external deployment owns the solution.

options.title: Broker-first core boundary
options.body: Define a narrow broker-backed capability contract that injects credentials only at dispatch time and keeps plaintext outside model/tool arguments and ambient agent environment.

options.title: External and plugin boundary
options.body: Document host isolation and credential-provider plugins as the supported solution and avoid adding an agent-exec secret contract to core.

options.title: Exec defense-in-depth only
options.body: Add narrowly scoped named-environment removal and exact-value redaction while documenting that it is not credential isolation.

recommendation.title: Broker-first core boundary
recommendation.body: Define a narrow broker-backed capability contract that injects credentials only at dispatch time and keeps plaintext outside model/tool arguments and ambient agent environment.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sets the security boundary for secret resolution, process execution, and plugin-facing credential access.
